newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED STABLE TO FIRMER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED STABLE TO FIRMER.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer in quiet trade on Tuesday, dealers said.

The market opened with a Z$65.4 million surplus and the central Reserve Bank, forecasting another surplus with Z$550 million treasury bills maturing on Tuesday, sold Z$600 million worth of 91-day treasury bills at 25 percent, slightly up from 24.99 percent the previous day.
Treausury bills were being traded on the secondary market at a stable 24.65 percent as was call money at 22 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills edged up to 25.35 from 25.25 percent (buying) and to 24.85 from 24.75 percent (selling).
The buying rate quoted for 30-, 60- and 90-day NCD bills was unchanged at 26 percent, but they were being sold firmer at 25.5 from 25 percent.
